_comment: The target journal's front-matter limits, as machine-readable data rather than
numbers typed into a checker. Every entry carries the sentence it came from, so
the limit and its evidence cannot drift apart. Read by tools/check_frontmatter.py
and tools/check_submission_ready.py; nothing here is duplicated in code.
To re-verify: open the URL below, find each quoted sentence, and update BOTH the
value and the quote together. Then set verified.date to the day you did it.
Changing a value without changing its quote is the failure this file prevents.

source.note: The journal's own guide, not a summary of it and not a general Elsevier page.

verified.by: fetched from the URL above and read for each quoted sentence
note: This is the date the limits below were last read at the source. It is not a
claim that they are current today. A guide for authors changes without notice,
so tools/check_submission_ready.py reports this entry as PENDING once it is
older than recheck_after_days, and re-verification is a pre-submission item.

_comment: Requirements read at the same source and in the same pass, which this checker
deliberately does not test. They are listed so that the absence of a check is a
recorded decision rather than an oversight, and so that the next person to read
the guide can see what was already read.

abstract_structure.quote: You are required to provide a concise and factual abstract which does not exceed 250 words.
abstract_structure.why: The guide states a length and a character ('concise and factual'); it does not require a structured abstract and does not forbid one. Earlier drafts of this repository asserted 'and unstructured' as a journal requirement. That was not in the guide. The abstract here is narrative, which the guide permits, but it is a choice and is no longer recorded as a rule.

article_words.quote: Full papers, describing original work, i.e. the technical development and the clinical / experimental study to prove the concept / value of a novel technique and should normally be about 5,000 words.
silent_on: The guide does not say whether the 5,000 words include or exclude tables, figure
captions, references, the abstract or supplementary material. Re-read at the source
on 30 September 2026 specifically to settle that question, and it is not settled
there. This repository therefore reports the article's length BOTH ways and treats
no_stated_penalty: The guide states no page limit, no excess-length charge and no consequence for
exceeding the recommended length. 'Should normally be about' is guidance. That is
not a licence to run long; it means a longer paper is an editorial judgement rather
than a desk-reject rule, and the judgement is the editor's.
article_words.why: 'Normally about' is guidance, not a limit. Reported by tools/check_split_map.py as information; never a failure.

provenance: HOW THIS WAS OBTAINED, stated exactly, because it is weaker than every other
entry in this file and it is the requirement this repository acts on hardest.
The sentence below was written into this project on 4 October 2026, as read from
the guide, in the working script that became tools/build_docx.py. That script
lived outside the repository until 7 October 2026, so until this entry existed
the requirement that caused a whole build tool to be written was recorded
NOWHERE in the package -- which is why it is recorded here now.
It was NOT re-read at the source on 7 October 2026: a fetch of the guide was
refused from this environment, as it was on 2 October 2026, and a web search did
not surface the sentence. So the wording has one source, taken on one day, and no
second reading.
CONSEQUENCE: nothing is enforced on it, and confirming this sentence by eye in a
browser is a pre-submission item alongside re-reading the limits above.
manuscript_source_file.quote: Save files in an editable format, using the extension .doc/.docx for Word files and .tex for LaTeX files. A PDF is not an acceptable source file.
why: Acted upon rather than checked. No script can usefully test 'the file you upload
is editable'; what the repository can do is produce one, so tools/build_docx.py
builds the .docx from the same twelve section files the PDF is built from.
This is also why tools/build_pdf.py is no longer the end of the line. The PDF
remains the file to READ and to cite a page of; the .docx is the file to SUBMIT.
manuscript/REPRODUCIBILITY.md section 1 said the PDF was the only file to review,
cite or submit, which was written before this sentence was read and was corrected

highlights_separate_file.quote: Submit highlights as a separate editable file in the online submission system.
highlights_separate_file.why: A packaging requirement of the submission system, not of the text. The highlights live in manuscript/ABSTRACT.md so they stay with the paper they summarise; producing the separate file is a submission-packaging step.

graphical_abstract_pixels.quote: Ensure the image is 531 x 1328 pixels (h x w) or proportionally more, and is readable at a size of 5 x 13 cm.
graphical_abstract_pixels.why: Optional for this journal, and not drafted. If one is added it becomes a figure check, not a front-matter check.

quote: Bitmapped line drawings: Minimum resolution 1000 dpi (min. width: single column: 3543 pixels; full page: 7480 pixels)
Photographs (color or grayscale): Minimum resolution 300 dpi (min. width: single column: 1063 pixels; full page: 2244 pixels)
figure_resolution.why: A property of the figure files, not of the front matter. Belongs to the print-ready figure check, which is not yet written.

reference_style.value: numbered, square brackets, order of appearance
quote: Indicate references by adding a number within square brackets in the text.
Number references in the order they appear in your article.
reference_style.why: Checked by tools/check_crossrefs.py against manuscript/REFERENCES.md, which is where citation order is resolvable.

quote: We encourage the use of supplementary materials such as applications, images and sound clips to enhance research.
Submit all supplementary materials at the same time as your manuscript.
Include a concise, descriptive caption for each supplementary file.
After submission supplementary files can only be added or replaced in the revision stage of the editorial process.
Be aware that all supplementary materials provided will appear online in the exact same way as received. These files will not be checked, formatted or typeset by the production team.
why: Three operational consequences, recorded because each one is a way to lose work at
submission. The supplementary file must be FINISHED when the manuscript is submitted,
not added later. It must carry its own caption. And it is published exactly as sent and
is never typeset, so manuscript/SUPPLEMENTARY.md must be delivered as a laid-out PDF
rather than as a source file.

article_title.quote: Article titles should be concise and informative. Please avoid abbreviations and formulae, where possible, unless they are established and widely understood, e.g. DNA.
silent_on: The guide states NO title length limit, in words or characters.
The guide states NO capitalization rule: neither title case nor sentence case is
prescribed or forbidden. Read at the source on 2 October 2026 specifically to settle
that question, because a title change was under consideration, and it is not settled
there. So the capitalization of this paper's title is an author choice, like the
licence, and must not be recorded or argued as a journal requirement.
why: There is no value to enforce. The one substantive rule -- avoid abbreviations unless
established and widely understood -- is satisfied: the only abbreviation in the title
is EEG, which sits in the same class as the guide's own example, DNA.

quote: Provide the given name(s) and family name(s) of each author.
Indicate affiliations using a lower-case superscript letter.
Present the full name and postal address of each affiliation, including the country name.
Clearly indicate who will handle correspondence.
The email address of the corresponding author must be included on the title page and will be published.
A 'present address' (or 'permanent address') can be indicated by a footnote.
required_elements: each author's given name(s) and family name(s), in submission order
each affiliation's full name and postal address including the country, marked with a lower-case superscript letter
which author handles correspondence, indicated clearly
the corresponding author's email address -- mandatory, and it is published

note: The guide states NO requirement for a telephone number on the title page. This is
recorded because the opposite was asserted in this project on 1 and 2 October 2026
-- a telephone number was listed as a thing the author had to supply -- from the
general Elsevier convention rather than from this journal's guide. It was read at
the source on 2 October 2026 and is not there. Do not ask for it again.

why: A packaging requirement of the submission, not of the manuscript text, and the title
page does not exist yet. It is recorded here so that building it needs no guesswork:
the only thing still missing from the repository is each affiliation's postal address.
